titleEn: The Song of the Cid — Raids from the hill; Minaya returns with men; the count of Barcelona takes offence (tiradas 49–55, lines 899–959)
part: Tiradas 49–55 · Raids from the hill; Minaya returns with men; the count of Barcelona takes offence (lines 899–959)

sentences.t:
Quiérovos dezir del que en buen[a] çinxo espada:
aquel poyo en él priso posada;
mientra que sea el pueblo de moros e de la yente cristiana,
el Poyo de mio Çid asil dirán por carta.
sentences.i: I would tell you of him who girded on his sword in a good hour: on that hill he made his camp, and for as long as there are Moors and Christian folk in the world, it will be called in writing the Poyo of my Çid.
sentences.n: Tirada 49 (assonance á-a) — the Çid's raids from the Poyo; Minaya with two hundred Castilians rejoins the Çid (Pidal: Correrías del Cid desde el Poyo. — Minaya con doscientos castellanos se reúne al Cid). The line-ends are á-a again (espada, posada, cristiana, carta, preava, paria …). The minstrel turns from the king's court back to the Çid. Quiérovos = quiero + vos, 'I want … to you' (the dative glued on the verb). del que en buen[a] çinxo espada, 'of him who girded on his sword in a good hour', the epic formula for the Çid; çinxo, old strong preterite of çeñir; the a of buena is in italics, Pidal's restoration (buena beside the usual buen ora). Note that ora, 'hour', is not written: en buena stands for en buena ora, the noun understood, so the formula is complete in sense; the l line supplies it as 'a-good (hour)', as in the earlier parts. aquel poyo, the hill above Monreal where the last part left him (v. 864); en él, 'on it', resumes it. priso, 'took', old preterite of prender (modern prendió/tomó); posada, 'lodging, camp'. Pidal: v. 901 is an adverbial phrase meaning 'as long as the world lasts, always' (compare v. 145); mientra que = mientras que; yente = gente. asil = así le, 'so … it' (le, the hill). por carta: Pidal, 'por escrito', 'in writing'. Pidal adds that the minstrel's prophecy failed: the name whose eternity the poem foretells was soon lost, though it is still used in the Fuero de Molina (see his note on v. 864).

sentences.t:
Estando allí, mucha tierra preava,
el [val] de río Martín todo lo metió en paria.
sentences.l:
Being there, much land he-was-plundering,
the [vale] of river Martín all it he-put in tribute.
sentences.i: While he was there he plundered much land, and the whole valley of the river Martín he put under tribute.
sentences.n: preava, 'plundered, raided' (prear, from Latin praeda, 'booty'), imperfect, then the preterite metió: epic tense-mixing. Pidal here refers to his note on v. 477. el [val] de río Martín: the word val, 'valley', is in italics, supplied by Pidal. Pidal gives no note on the river. todo lo, 'all of it', the object said twice. metió en paria, 'put under tribute' (paria, the protection-money paid by a Moorish town), as with Daroca and the other towns before.

sentences.t:
A Saragoça sus nuevas legavan,
non plaze a los moros, firme mientre les pesava.
sentences.l:
To Saragoça his news they-were-arriving,
not it-pleases the Moors, firm-ly to-them it-was-grieving.
sentences.i: News of him kept reaching Zaragoza; it did not please the Moors there, it weighed on them sorely.
sentences.n: Saragoça, Zaragoza, seat of the Moorish kingdom to which these towns belonged. legavan = llegavan, 'were arriving', printed with a single l: kept as printed. non plaze, present, beside the imperfect pesava. firme mientre, 'firmly, sorely': the adverb in -mientre (modern -mente) still written as two words, the adjective plus the noun 'mind'. les pesava, 'it grieved them' (pesar, 'to weigh on').

sentences.t: Allí sovo mio Çid conplidas quinze se[d]manas;
sentences.l: There stayed my Çid full fifteen weeks;
sentences.i: My Çid stayed there fifteen full weeks;
sentences.n: sovo, 'was, stayed', old preterite of seer (= estuvo). conplidas, 'full, complete' (cumplidas). se[d]manas = semanas, 'weeks', the d in italics, Pidal's restoration (the old form sedmana, from Latin septimana).

sentences.i: when the worthy man saw that Minaya was long in coming, he made a night march with all his people; he left the Poyo and abandoned it altogether,
sentences.n: el caboso, 'the excellent one, the worthy man': Pidal, 'el Cid' (v. 226, where it is rendered 'the worthy man'). vío = vio, 'saw', accented as printed. se tardava, 'was delaying, was slow' (tardarse). yentes = gentes. trasnochada, 'a march through the night' (trasnochar, 'to pass the night', here 'to march by night'). dexó = dejó, 'left'. desenparava, 'abandoned, left unprotected' (desamparar); imperfect beside preterite again. Note that at v. 938, after the Alcañiz raid, Pidal reads the Çid as returning to the Poyo.

sentences.t:
allén de Teruel don Rodrigo passava,
en el pinar de Tévar Roy Díaz posava;
todas essas tierras todas las preava,
a Saragoça metuda lâ en paria.
sentences.l:
beyond Teruel don Rodrigo was-passing,
in the pine-wood of Tévar Roy Díaz was-lodging;
all those lands all them he-was-plundering,
to Saragoça put her-has in tribute.
sentences.i: Don Rodrigo passed on beyond Teruel and made his camp in the pine-wood of Tévar; all those lands he plundered, and Zaragoza he has put under tribute.
sentences.n: allén de, 'beyond'. don Rodrigo and Roy Díaz are the Çid's own name, Rodrigo Díaz: Roy = Ruy, the short form of Rodrigo. Here Roy is printed all in roman type, whereas at vv. 942 and 958 Pidal prints R[o]y with the o in italics as his restoration: kept as printed in each place. pinar, 'pine-wood'. Tévar: Pidal refers to his note on v. 971, where the pine-wood returns. todas essas tierras todas las, 'all those lands, all of them', the object announced and taken up again. 914 lâ: so printed by Pidal (checked on the scan: a circumflex on the a). It is read here as la + a (ha), 'has her/it', the circumflex marking two a's run together: metuda lâ = la ha metido, 'he has put it', with the old participle metuda (-udo, as metudo in the sale of Alcocer) agreeing with the feminine object; a Saragoça, the object marked by a, would then be Zaragoza itself put under tribute, which fits v. 941, where the men of Zaragoza pay parias. Pidal gives no footnote on the line, so the analysis of lâ (and whether la refers to Zaragoza or to the lands) is uncertain.

sentences.t:
Quando esto fecho ovo, a cabo de tres se[d]manas
de Castiella venido es Minaya,
dozientos con él, que todos çiñen espadas;
non son en cuenta, sabet, las peonadas.
sentences.i: When this was done, at the end of three weeks, Minaya has come from Castile, with two hundred men, every one of them girded with a sword; and the foot-soldiers, I tell you, are not counted.
sentences.n: fecho ovo, 'he had done' (fecho = hecho, f- for h-; ovo, preterite of aver, as auxiliary). se[d]manas, the d again Pidal's. venido es, 'has come': verbs of motion form their perfect with ser. que todos çiñen espadas, 'who all gird swords', i.e. two hundred knights. non son en cuenta, 'are not in the reckoning'. sabet = sabed, 'know', the minstrel's aside to his listeners. peonadas, 'bands of foot-soldiers' (peón).

sentences.t:
Quando vi[d]o mio Çid asomar a Minaya,
el cavallo corriendo, valo abraçar sin falla,
besóle la boca e los ojos de la cara.
sentences.l:
When saw my Çid appear Minaya,
the horse running, goes-him to-embrace without fail,
he-kissed-him the mouth and the eyes of the face.
sentences.i: When my Çid saw Minaya come into view, he rode at the gallop and went to embrace him without delay; he kissed him on the mouth and on the eyes of his face.
sentences.n: vi[d]o = vio, 'saw', from the old preterite vido; the d is Pidal's. asomar, 'to come into sight, appear'; a Minaya, the personal object with a. el cavallo corriendo, 'the horse running', an absolute construction: at full gallop. valo abraçar = va lo abraçar, 'he goes to embrace him', the pronoun lo glued to va. sin falla, 'without fail', a filler formula. besóle, 'he kissed him' (besó + le). los ojos de la cara, 'the eyes of the face', a stock epic fullness.

sentences.t: Todo gelo dize, que nol encubre nada.
sentences.l: All to-him-it he-tells, that not-to-him he-hides nothing.
sentences.i: He tells him everything, keeping nothing from him.
sentences.n: gelo = se lo, 'it to him' (the old form of the dative before lo). nol = no le, 'not … from him', the le squeezed onto non. Double negative non … nada. The subject is Minaya, giving his report of the king's answer; the present tense after the preterites.

sentences.i: The Campeador smiled most graciously: “Thanks be to God and to His holy powers! As long as you live, Minaya, things will go well with me!”
sentences.n: fermoso, 'handsomely, beautifully' (hermoso), an adjective used as an adverb, as when the king smiled at Minaya's gift. sonrrisava, double rr as printed. grado a Dios, 'thanks to God' (grado, 'gratitude'). las sus vertudes santas, 'His holy virtues', i.e. powers, article + possessive. mientra = mientras. visquiéredes, 'you may live', future subjunctive of bivir (vivir), built on the old strong preterite visque. bien me irá a mí, 'it will go well with me', the pronoun doubled (me … a mí) for emphasis. In Pidal's print the last word is broken Mi-, with naya!” set at the end of the line above; here it is put back in its line.

sentences.t:
¡Dios, cómmo f[o] alegre todo aquel fonssado,
que Minaya Álvar Fáñez assi era llegado,
diziéndoles saludes de primos e de hermanos,
e de sus compañas, aquellas que avien dexad[o]!
sentences.l:
God, how was glad all that host,
that Minaya Álvar Fáñez thus was arrived,
telling-them greetings from cousins and from brothers,
and from their households, those which they-had left!
sentences.i: God, how glad the whole host was that Minaya Álvar Fáñez had come in this way, bringing them news of their cousins and brothers, and of the households they had left behind!
sentences.n: Tirada 50 (assonance á-o) — joy of the exiles at receiving news from Castile (Pidal: Alegría de los desterrados al recibir noticias de Castilla). The line-ends are á-o (fonssado, llegado, hermanos, dexado). f[o] = fue, 'was', the old preterite fo shared by ser and ir; the o is in italics, Pidal's. fonssado: Pidal, 'ejército', 'army' (compare v. 764). Álvar is printed here with v (Álvar), as at v. 934, whereas vv. 931 and 945 print Álbar with b: both kept as printed. era llegado, 'had arrived', the pluperfect of a verb of motion with ser. saludes: Pidal, 'news of an absent person' (compare v. 1921), more than mere greetings. compañas, 'companies, people': here the households and kin left behind in Castile (no footnote; the sense is ours). avien dexad[o] = habían dejado, 'they had left' (avien, old imperfect in -ie); the final o is Pidal's.

sentences.t:
Dios, cómmo es alegre la barba vellida,
que Álbar Fáñez pagó las mill missas,
e quel dixo saludes de su mugier e de sus fijas!
sentences.l:
God, how is glad the beard handsome,
that Álbar Fáñez paid the thousand masses,
and that-to-him he-told greetings from his wife and from his daughters!
sentences.i: God, how glad is he of the handsome beard, that Álvar Fáñez has paid for the thousand masses and brought him news of his wife and his daughters!
sentences.n: Tirada 51 (assonance í-a) — the Çid's joy, a twin series (Pidal: Alegría del Cid. (Serie gemela.)). The new assonance í-a (vellida, missas, fijas, alegría, días, mandadería) carries a twin of tirada 50: the same joy told again, now the Çid's own. la barba vellida, 'he of the handsome beard': Pidal, 'el Cid' (compare v. 274, where it is rendered so); vellida, 'handsome, fair' (bello). Álbar Fáñez, with b, as printed (Álvar at vv. 927 and 934). pagó las mill missas: the thousand masses at Santa María of Burgos that the Çid vowed at v. 225 and charged Minaya to pay for when he sent him to Castile (v. 822). quel = que le, 'that … to him'. saludes, 'news' of the absent, as v. 928. mugier, 'wife'; fijas = hijas, 'daughters' (f- for h-): Jimena and the girls, left at San Pedro de Cardeña.

sentences.t: Dios, cómmo f[o] el Çid pagado e fizo grant alegría!
sentences.l: God, how was the Çid pleased and made great joy!
sentences.i: God, how pleased the Çid was, and how he rejoiced!
sentences.n: f[o] = fue, 'was', again with the o in Pidal's italics. pagado, 'pleased, satisfied' (pagar, 'to please'). fizo grant alegría, 'made great rejoicing' (fizo = hizo, f- for h-).

sentences.t:
“Ya Álvar Fáñez, bivades muchos días!
más valedes que nos, ¡tan buena mandadería!”
sentences.l:
“O Álvar Fáñez, may-you-live many days!
more are-worth you than we, so good errand!”
sentences.i: “Álvar Fáñez, long may you live! You are worth more than we are — so fine an embassy!”
sentences.n: Ya, 'O', a vocative particle (as in ya cavalleros, v. 947). Álvar with v, as printed. bivades = viváis, 'may you live' (subjunctive of a wish). The second line, 934b, is printed wholly in italics by Pidal: it is his restoration, not the manuscript's, and is printed here in plain type; it has no number in his margin, and the letter b is a provisional number of ours. valedes, 'you are worth' (valer). nos, 'we', unaccented as printed. mandadería, 'embassy, errand', the mission Minaya has carried out (mandado, 'message').

sentences.i: He who was born in a good hour made no delay: he took two hundred knights, picked by hand, and rode out on a raid, marching through the night;
sentences.n: Tirada 52 (assonance á-o) — the Çid raids the lands of Alcañiz (Pidal: El Cid corre tierras de Alcañiz). The line-ends are á-o (nasco, mano, trasnochando, parando, preando, tornado). Non lo tardó, 'he did not delay it'. nasco, 'was born', old strong preterite of nacer: el que en buen ora nasco, the 'born in a good hour' formula. The two lines that follow are printed wholly in italics by Pidal: they are his restoration, printed here in plain type. Neither has a number in Pidal's margin; the first is numbered 935b only in his footnote ('935 b escollecho …'), so that label is his; the second has no number anywhere in his print, and the letter c is provisional, ours. escollechos: Pidal, a dialectal participle, used by the Crónica General, instead of escogido, 'chosen'. a mano, 'by hand'. corrida, 'raid, foray' (correr, 'to overrun'). la noch trasnochando, 'marching through the night'.

sentences.t:
tierras d'Alcañiz negras las va parando,
e a derredor todo lo va preando.
sentences.l:
lands of-Alcañiz black them he-goes leaving,
and round-about all it he-goes plundering.
sentences.i: the lands of Alcañiz he leaves waste and barren, and all around he plunders everything.
sentences.n: d'Alcañiz, 'of Alcañiz' (Pidal gives no note on the place). negras: Pidal, 'yermas, estériles', 'waste, barren', as opposed to tierra blanca, sown land. va parando, 'goes leaving': ir + gerund for a continuing action; parar, 'to put in a state, leave (something) so'. las and lo take up the objects already named. a derredor, 'round about' (alrededor). preando, 'plundering', as v. 903.

sentences.t: Al terçer día, don ixo i es tornado.
sentences.l: On-the third day, whence he-went-out there is returned.
sentences.i: On the third day he is back where he set out from.
sentences.n: terçer = tercer. don = de donde, 'whence'; ixo, 'went out', old preterite of exir (salir); i, 'there'; es tornado, 'has returned', ser with a verb of motion. Pidal: 'donde salió allá se tornó', that is, he went back to the Poyo of my Çid.

sentences.t:
Hya va el mandado por las tierras todas,
pesando va a los de Monçon e a los de Hu[o]sca;
sentences.l:
Now goes the news through the lands all,
grieving it-goes to those of Monçon and to those of Hu[o]sca;
sentences.i: Now the news is going through all the lands; it grieves the men of Monzón and of Huesca;
sentences.n: Tirada 53 (assonance ó-a) — the Moors are taught a lesson (Pidal: Escarmiento de los moros). The line-ends are ó-a (todas, Huosca, Saragoça, fonta). Hya = ya, 'now, already', with the scribe's h. mandado, 'message, news'. pesando va, 'goes grieving', i.e. it grieves (ir + gerund). Monçon: Pidal, Monzón is a town and castle south-east of Huesca, between that town and Balaguer. Hu[o]sca, Huesca, with the old diphthong uo; the o is in italics, Pidal's.

sentences.t:
por que dan parias plaze a los de Saragoça,
de mio Çid R[o]y Díaz que non temién ninguna fonta.
sentences.l:
because they-give tributes it-pleases those of Saragoça,
of my Çid R[o]y Díaz that not they-were-fearing any harm.
sentences.i: because they pay tribute, the men of Zaragoza are glad: they had no fear of any harm from my Çid Ruy Díaz.
sentences.n: por que, 'because'. parias, 'tributes', the protection-money (v. 914). plaze, 'it pleases'; the men of Zaragoza are content, since their tribute shields them while their neighbours are raided. temién = temían, old imperfect in -ié. ninguna fonta, 'any harm': Pidal, fonta, 'ultraje', 'daño' en general, 'outrage', 'harm' in general; non … ninguna, double negative. R[o]y, only the o in Pidal's italics (Roy in roman at v. 912).

sentences.i: With these winnings they go back to camp; all are glad, for great are the spoils they bring; it pleased my Çid, and Álvar Fáñez greatly.
sentences.n: Tirada 54 (assonance á) — the Çid abandons the Poyo and raids lands under the protection of the count of Barcelona (Pidal: El Cid abandona el Poyo. — Corre tierras amparadas por el Conde de Barcelona). The assonance is a single stressed á (van, endurar, verdad, menguar, Alucat, mal …); grandes, Fáñez and partes end in á-e, the unstressed final e not counting. ganançias, 'gains, booty'. la posada, 'the camp'. tornando se van, 'they go returning', ir + gerund. Pidal prints a full stop after van although todos follows in lower case (checked on the scan at 600 dpi: a round full stop, not a comma): kept as printed, and the sense runs on. plogo = plugo, 'it pleased' (old preterite of plazer). Álbar with b, as printed.

sentences.t: Sonrrisós el caboso, que non lo pudo endurar:
sentences.l: Smiled-himself the excellent-one, that not it he-could endure:
sentences.i: The worthy man smiled, for he could not spare them what was coming:
sentences.n: Sonrrisós = sonrrisó + se, 'he smiled' (the se glued on). el caboso, the Çid (v. 908). endurar: Pidal, 'resistir', 'to resist, hold off'; the sense, he says, is that the Çid could not spare his men the hardship of the immediate march he now announces; he recalls that in the Poema de Fernán González (st. 333) the count's vassals complain of being forever on campaign. The line is hard: lo, 'it', is the march (or the men's discomfort), and the reading is Pidal's.

sentences.t:
“ya cavalleros, dezir vos he la verdad:
qui en un logar mora siempre, lo so puede menguar;
cras a la mañana penssemos de cavalgar,
dexat estas posadas e iremos adelant.”
sentences.l:
“O knights, to-say to-you I-will the truth:
who in one place stays always, the his-own can dwindle;
tomorrow at the morning let-us-think to ride,
leave these lodgings and we-will-go forward.”
sentences.i: “Knights, I will tell you the truth: he who always stays in one place may see his substance dwindle. Tomorrow in the morning let us be riding; leave these quarters, and we will go on ahead.”
sentences.n: ya cavalleros, 'O knights'. dezir vos he, 'I will tell you': the split future, infinitive + pronoun + he (= os diré). qui = quien, 'he who'; mora, 'dwells, stays' (morar). lo so = lo suyo, 'what is his own', 'his substance' (so, the old possessive, as sos in v. 1): so the words read grammatically; Pidal has no footnote on lo so. menguar, 'to diminish, run short'. cras, 'tomorrow' (Latin cras), a la mañana, 'in the morning'. penssemos de cavalgar, 'let us set about riding' (pensar de + infinitive, as v. 10). dexat = dejad, imperative. iremos adelant, 'we will go onward'.

sentences.i: Then the Çid shifted his camp to the pass of Alucat; from there my Çid raids as far as Huesa and Montalbán; on that foray they spent ten days.
sentences.n: Estonçes = entonces. se mudó, 'moved (camp)'. puerto, 'mountain pass'. Pidal: Alucat is today Olocau del Rey, 15 km west of Morella, on the western edge of the province of Castellón; Olocau is 50 and 65 km from Montalbán and Huesa, both towns of the province of Teruel. Huesa is not Huesca. dent = de ende, 'from there'. corre, 'raids, overruns' (correr la tierra). aquessa = esa; dias unaccented as printed. ovieron a morar, 'they had to stay, they stayed' (aver a + infinitive).

sentences.t:
F[o]ron los mandados a todas partes,
que el salido de Castiella así los trae tan mal.
sentences.l:
Went the messages to all parts,
that the gone-out from Castiella thus them treats so badly.
sentences.i: Word went out in every direction that the exile from Castile was handling them so roughly.
sentences.n: F[o]ron = fueron, 'went', from ir (fo, foron, shared by ir and ser); the o is Pidal's. mandados, 'messages, news'. el salido: Pidal, as at v. 981, it means 'expatriate, exile', 'the man gone out' of Castile. los trae tan mal, 'treats them so badly' (traer, 'to handle, treat'); los, the people of those lands.

sentences.t: Los mandados son idos a [las] partes todas;
sentences.l: The messages are gone to [the] parts all;
sentences.i: The news has gone out to every part;
sentences.n: Tirada 55 (assonance ó-a) — threats of the count of Barcelona (Pidal: Amenazas del conde de Barcelona). The line-ends are ó-a (todas, Barçilona, toda, fonta), and the tirada repeats the end of the last one in the new assonance. son idos, 'have gone', ser with a verb of motion. [las], the article, is in italics, supplied by Pidal.

sentences.i: the tidings reached the count of Barcelona that my Çid Ruy Díaz was overrunning all his land; he was sorely grieved, and took it as a great affront.
sentences.n: co[m]de = conde, 'count', the m in italics, Pidal's restoration. Barçilona, Barcelona, as printed. que … quel: the que is said twice, 'that … that' (quel = que le, 'that … to him', the dative of the person harmed). corrié = corría, old imperfect in -ié; correr la tierra, 'to raid the land'. R[o]y, only the o Pidal's. Pidal: these were not properly the count's lands but lands under his protectorate (compare v. 964): the lands of the Moorish king of Lérida, Alhagib Monzir, protected by Berenguer Ramón, 'the Fratricide' (his introduction, pp. 15–16). ovo, 'had' (aver). tóvoslo = tovo + se + lo, 'he held it' (tener, old preterite tovo), tener a, 'to consider as'. fonta: Pidal, 'ultraje, afrenta', 'outrage, affront'.
